en: [Siddham] Homage to Mañjunātha!
In the accomplishment of the deity, six limbs are to be known as taught by the Victor:
meditative absorption, cultivation, recitation, hymn of praise, worship, and prostration.

Then, having become supremely pure in a place conducive to practice, the mantra-practitioner, seated on a low seat, should purify excellent molasses and divine water three times with this mantra: OṂ ĀḤ VAJRODAKE AMṚTĪBHAVA HŪṂ SVĀHĀ.
Taking this,
just as all the Tathāgatas were bathed immediately upon their birth,
so shall I bathe you with pure, divine water.
Oṃ āḥ, for the glory of the commitment of the empowerment of all Tathāgatas, hūṃ. This is the bathing mantra.

Then, for the sake of purifying the six Tathāgatas, one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) upon the six sense faculties with the syllables *hrīṃ*, *trāṃ*, *oṃ*, *hūṃ*, *khaṃ*, and *vaṃ*. Having first uttered these six seed-syllables in sequence over the mouth, nose, eyes, ears, body, and heart, and having touched them with the tips of the five fingers, one should perform breath control (*prāṇāyāma*).
With *oṃ vaḥ svāhā*, one performs the sprinkling of the hands and feet.

With *oṃ hrīḥ svāhā*, one performs the ritual rinsing (*ācamana*). With *oṃ namo bhagavate puṣpaketuprabharājāya tathāgatāyārhate samyaksambuddhāya tadyathā oṃ 2 puṣpe puṣpe mahāpuṣpe supuṣpe puṣpodbhave puṣpasambhave puṣpāvakīrṇe svāhā*, one purifies the flowers seven times.
Then, taking a single flower with the left thumb and ring finger, one should perform the consecration of body, speech, and mind with: OṂ ĀḤ HŪṂ.

In the same way, taking a single flower, one should recite: *oṃ maṇidhari vajriṇi mahāpratisare rakṣa rakṣa māṃ sarvasattvāṃś ca hūṃ hūṃ phaṭ phaṭ svāhā*. With this, one should perform self-protection upon the head.
Oṃ subhūme vajrībhava hūṃ. Having sprinkled the ground of the maṇḍala to be constructed with this [mantra], one should purify it.
Then, with the mantra *oṃ vajrasattva sarvavighnān utsāraya utsāraya hūṃ phaṭ*, one should expel the obstructors by circling counter-clockwise.

Then, while smearing a circular maṇḍala with cow dung from which the life-force has departed, mixed with water and fragrant sandalwood and so forth, using the right hand and circling clockwise, one should recite two verses.
Charity is cow dung mixed with water; ethical discipline is sweeping; patience is the removal of small ants; vigor is the exertion of activity;
meditation is making the mind one-pointed for that moment; and wisdom is the bright, well-drawn lines.
Having constructed the maṇḍala of the Sage, one obtains these very six perfections.
He becomes golden-hued, liberated from all diseases, and distinguished among gods and men with a radiant splendor like the moon;
he is born into a royal lineage, enriched with wealth and gold.
Having performed bodily actions within this supreme abode of the Sugata,
Then, having placed the right thumb in the center of the smeared mandala, [one should visualize] with the index finger as if it were a full moon disc.
Oṃ vajrarekhe surekhe hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. One should draw the lines in a clockwise direction.
Taking a single flower with the left hand and placing that flower on the back of the right hand, one should cover the hand while reciting:
"Oṃ surekhe, may all the Tathāgatas empower [this]; svāhā! Then, one should offer that flower in the center of the maṇḍala.
Then, having washed one's hands and taken a flower with both the left and right hands, one should consecrate the maṇḍala with: *oṃ candrārkavimale svāhā*.

Having visualized that maṇḍala in the form of the moon and sun, one should contemplate the syllable *dhīḥ* within a moon maṇḍala transformed from the syllable *a* at one’s own heart; then, having illuminated the Blessed One in the sky with a network of its rays, one should invoke him.

With this mantra—*oṃ śaradamalamadhyāhnagaganopama dharmadhātusvabhāva bhagavan mañjughoṣa ihāgaccha ihāgaccha maṇḍale 'dhiṣṭhānaṃ kuru jaḥ hūṃ vaṃ hoḥ*—one should summon [the deity] into the maṇḍala and cause him to bestow his blessing. Having made him well-bound and well-pleased, one should offer: *oṃ pravarasatkāra śrīmañjughoṣa arghapādyāsanācamanaprokṣaṇaṃ pratīccha svāhā*. Then, with a single-pointed mind and through an excess of faith, one should perform the worship.
In the center: Oṃ arapacanāya vajrapuṣpe dhīḥ svāhā.
In front: Oṃ jālinīprabhāya svāhā.
In the back: Oṃ candraprabhāyai vajrapuṣpe paṃ svāhā.
On the right: *Oṃ keśinyai vajrapuṣpe caṃ svāhā*.
On the left: *Oṃ upakeśinyai vajrapuṣpe naṃ svāhā*.
Having worshipped them with their respective mantras using flowers, incense, lamps, perfumes, food offerings, and so forth, one should present the *bali* offering with the *bali* mantra.

Oṃ, the syllable *A* is the gateway to all phenomena because they are unproduced from the very beginning. Oṃ Āḥ Hūṃ Hoḥ! With this, one should purify the *bali* offering. Then: Oṃ, to Arapacana, who is skilled at burning away ignorance, who possesses the luster of a moonstone gem, whose foremost hands are occupied with a sword and a book, and who bestows the boon of Mañjughoṣa’s speech: accept, accept this *bali*, perfume, flower, incense, lamp, along with honey, sugar, and so forth; *kha kha khāhi khāhi* (eat, eat)! Grant me peace, nourishment, protection, defense, and concealment! Oṃ Āḥ Dhīḥ Hūṃ Svāhā! This is the *bali* mantra.
Then one should recite this hymn:
"Whatever evil has been committed by me, who am of dull intellect,
that must be forgiven by you, O Protector, for you are the savior of all embodied beings."
Then, one should make a formal aspiration with this verse:
And by means of this merit, having attained the state of Buddhahood,
may I ferry across the entire world from the bottomless ocean of existence.
Then one should perform the dismissal with this verse:
The welfare of all sentient beings has been accomplished for you, and success has been granted according to your needs.
Go now to the realm of the Buddhas, so that you may return once more.
With your limbs anointed with the sandalwood of ethical discipline, clothed in the mantle of meditative concentration,
and strewn with the flowers of the factors of enlightenment, dwell at your ease.
Then one should recite the hundred-syllable king of mantras.

Oṃ! Vajrasattva, maintain the samaya; abide as Vajrasattva. Be firm for me, be well-pleased with me, be well-nourished by me, be devoted to me. Bestow upon me all siddhis, and in all actions, make my mind auspicious. Hūṃ ha ha ha ha hoḥ! O Blessed One, Vajra of all Tathāgatas, do not abandon me; become the Vajra, the Great Samayasattva! Āḥ!
Thus ends the ritual procedure for the worship of the venerable Arapacana Mañjunātha.

The ritual for the worship of White Mañjughoṣa Arapacana, composed by the master Ajitamitra, is complete. It was translated before the great paṇḍita Śrī Vanaratna by the monk Chos-’khor-lo-tsa-ba, and subsequently revised by the bhikṣu Rgya-mtsho.
*Namo Mañjunāthāya.* (Homage to the Lord Mañjuśrī. *Note: These verses [on folio 5r] were not published; NB: cf. Dhīḥ 19, which contains a very corrupt version.*

Beholding this world to be won over by affection, you carry it out of your total dependence on compassion— a display of intense passion, overflowing with the spreading beauty of the filaments of fresh saffron.
Between your two faces, which resemble a new cloud and the moon, there shines that which dwells within.
Your face possesses the loveliness of a golden lotus anointed with the light of the rising sun; 2.

You bear upon your head a radiance whose limbs are as beautiful as the spreading luster of spotless jewels set in ornaments, and which has the splendor of the color of a fresh cloud brightened by a circle of lightning. 3.
Adorned with the ornaments of auspicious marks, their splendor enhanced by the cries of ruddy geese at the touch of the morning rays— [the remaining eight verses are not available].
